title: utv package operations
description: The public entrypoints of the package: the typed layer's constructors, methods and functions, then the JSON layer's functions. Every one is a pure in-process call that changes nothing.

entities.name: Make a date
entities.description: CivilDate.of(year, month, day), or CivilDate(year, month, day): a proleptic Gregorian day with no zone. The year is any Python int. CivilDate.try_of returns an outcome instead of raising.
entities.result: The CivilDate; try_of gives Unique(CivilDate).
failures: The day doesn't exist in that month (30 February, 29 February in a common year): invalid (day-out-of-range). Constructors raise OutcomeError, a ValueError, with the status and diagnostics; try_of returns the same as an outcome.
The month is outside 1–12: invalid (month-out-of-range).
A field that isn't an int: TypeError.

entities.name: Make a month
entities.description: CivilYearMonth.of(year, month): a month of a year, with no day.
entities.result: The CivilYearMonth; try_of gives Unique(CivilYearMonth).
failures: The month is outside 1–12: invalid (month-out-of-range). Constructors raise OutcomeError, a ValueError, with the status and diagnostics; try_of returns the same as an outcome.
A field that isn't an int: TypeError.

entities.name: Make a time of day
entities.description: CivilTime.of(hour, minute[, second[, nanosecond]]): a wall-clock time that remembers whether a second was given (09:30 is not 09:30:00). A non-zero nanosecond without a second sets the second to 0.
entities.result: The CivilTime; try_of gives Unique(CivilTime).
failures: Hour, minute, second or nanosecond out of range: invalid (field-out-of-range). Constructors raise OutcomeError, a ValueError, with the status and diagnostics; try_of returns the same as an outcome.
Second 60: unsupported (leap-second); it needs a leap-second table.
24:00: unsupported (end-of-day); 24 with non-zero minutes or seconds is invalid (field-out-of-range).
A field that isn't an int: TypeError.

entities.name: Make a wall-clock date-time
entities.description: CivilDateTime.of(year, month, day, hour, minute[, second[, nanosecond]]), CivilDateTime(date, time) or date.at(time): a date and a time of day with no zone.
entities.result: The CivilDateTime; try_of gives Unique(CivilDateTime).
failures: Any failure of making the date or the time, with the same codes. Constructors raise OutcomeError, a ValueError, with the status and diagnostics; try_of returns the same as an outcome.
CivilDateTime(date, time) given anything but a CivilDate and a CivilTime: TypeError.

entities.name: Pin a wall time to an offset
entities.description: date_time.at_offset(seconds): the wall time at a fixed UTC offset, in seconds east of UTC. It names one instant without any zone rules.
entities.result: A FixedOffsetDateTime.
failures: The offset is beyond ±18:00: OutcomeError (invalid, offset-out-of-range).
The offset isn't an int: TypeError.

entities.name: Intend a wall time in a zone
entities.description: date_time.in_zone("Europe/Paris"): the wall time as an intention in an IANA zone. No rules are consulted, so the zone id is checked only for its shape.
entities.result: A ZonedIntent with no asserted offset.
failures: The zone id isn't shaped like Area/Location: OutcomeError (invalid, syntax).
The zone id isn't a str: TypeError.

entities.name: Make an instant from a clock reading
entities.description: Instant.from_unix_seconds(seconds[, nanoseconds]) or Instant.from_unix_nanoseconds(time.time_ns()): an exact moment on the POSIX timescale. The library never reads the clock; the caller passes the reading in.
entities.result: The Instant, holding exact rational seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z.
failures: An argument that isn't an int: TypeError.

entities.name: Make an amount
entities.description: Period.of(years=…, months=…, …) or Period.of_days(30) (also of_years, of_months, of_weeks, and Period(...)): calendar components. PosixSeconds.of(n[, d]) and ElapsedSeconds.of(n[, d]): exact POSIX or SI seconds.
entities.result: The Period, PosixSeconds or ElapsedSeconds; negate() gives the opposite amount.
failures: A component or numerator that isn't an int: TypeError.

entities.name: Make a range
entities.description: Interval.half_open(a, b), Interval.closed(a, b), or Interval.of(Bound.included(a) | Bound.excluded(a) | Bound.UNBOUNDED | Bound.UNKNOWN, …) over CivilDate or Instant points; try_of returns an outcome.
entities.result: The Interval; try_of gives Unique(Interval).
failures: The end is before the start: invalid (reversed-interval). Constructors raise OutcomeError, a ValueError, with the status and diagnostics; try_of returns the same as an outcome.
No point at all, such as Interval.of(Bound.UNBOUNDED, Bound.UNKNOWN): unsupported (unsupported-form).
A date at one end and an instant at the other: invalid (kind-mismatch).
A Bound of anything but a CivilDate or an Instant: TypeError.

entities.name: Add days or weeks to a date
entities.description: date.add_days(n) and date.add_weeks(n): total, through the JSON layer's add.
entities.result: The CivilDate n days (or weeks) later; n may be negative.

entities.name: Add wall-clock time to a date-time
entities.description: date_time.add_days / add_weeks / add_hours / add_minutes / add_seconds(n): wall-clock arithmetic carrying into days. There is no zone, so no DST.
entities.result: The later CivilDateTime: 23:30 + 2 hours is 01:30 the next day.

entities.name: Add months or years
entities.description: date.add_months(n) and date.add_years(n), also on CivilDateTime and ZonedIntent (add_months). Without a policy the answer may not exist; with MonthEnd.CONSTRAIN it clamps.
entities.transport: method of CivilDate, CivilDateTime and ZonedIntent
entities.result: Without a policy, Outcome: Unique(value). With MonthEnd.CONSTRAIN (or "constrain"), the value itself, clamped to the month's last day.
failures: The day is missing from the target month (31 January + 1 month): NoneOf (month-end).
A policy other than CONSTRAIN in the policy form, MonthEnd.REJECT included: ValueError, because rejecting is what the call without a policy does.

entities.name: Add a period
entities.description: value.add(period[, month_end]) on CivilDate, CivilDateTime and ZonedIntent. It always returns an outcome and takes either month-end policy.
entities.transport: method of CivilDate, CivilDateTime and ZonedIntent
entities.result: Unique(value).
failures: The day is missing after the month step and the policy is REJECT (the default): NoneOf (month-end).
Hours, minutes or seconds added to a CivilDate: Invalid (kind-mismatch).

entities.name: Count days between dates
entities.description: date.days_until(other): whole days from this date to other.
entities.result: An int, negative when other is earlier.

entities.name: Move a zoned wall time
entities.description: zoned.add_days / add_weeks / add_hours / add_minutes / add_seconds(n): the same zone, a later wall time. Turning it into an instant is resolve's job.
entities.result: A ZonedIntent with the new wall time and no asserted offset (the JSON layer reports offset-assertion-dropped, info).

entities.name: Add seconds to an instant
entities.description: instant.add(PosixSeconds) adds exactly; instant.add(ElapsedSeconds) would need a leap-second table.
entities.result: With PosixSeconds, the Instant itself; with ElapsedSeconds, an Outcome[Instant].
failures: ElapsedSeconds: Unsupported (needs-leap-seconds).
Any other argument: TypeError.

entities.name: Measure between instants
entities.description: instant.until(other): the exact POSIX seconds from this instant to other.
entities.result: A PosixSeconds holding an exact fraction, such as 14403/4 s.

entities.name: Turn an offset date-time into an instant
entities.description: fixed.to_instant(): the moment a wall time at a fixed offset names. No rules are needed.
entities.result: The Instant.

entities.name: See an instant at an offset
entities.description: instant.at_offset(seconds): the wall time at a fixed UTC offset at this instant.
entities.result: A FixedOffsetDateTime, always with seconds.
failures: The offset is beyond ±18:00: OutcomeError (invalid, offset-out-of-range).

entities.name: Load zone rules
entities.description: ZoneRules.load(path) reads a rule bundle from the file the caller names; ZoneRules.parse(text) parses JSON text or a dict. Same as load_rules / parse_rules.
entities.result: An immutable ZoneRules: the rule set's id and version, the validity window and each zone's transitions.
failures: Text that isn't JSON, a missing key or a wrong type (malformed rule bundle), transitions out of order or an offset beyond ±18:00: ValueError.
A file that can't be opened: the OSError of open().

entities.name: Hold the zone rules
entities.description: TemporalContext(rules) or TemporalContext.with_rules(rules). There is no default or global context.
entities.result: A TemporalContext that every zone operation is given.
failures: Anything but ZoneRules, such as a path: TypeError.

entities.name: Resolve a zoned wall time
entities.description: zoned.resolve(ctx[, policy]), the same as ctx.resolve(zoned, policy): the instant(s) a wall time names under the context's rules. The policy defaults to ResolutionPolicy.STRICT.
entities.result: Unique(Instant), or Multiple of both instants, ascending; to_result() carries the rule set in manifest.dependencies.
failures: The wall time falls in a gap and the gap policy is REJECT or PRESERVE_UNRESOLVED: NoneOf (gap).
The wall time falls in an overlap and the overlap policy is REJECT: Multiple (ambiguous); with ALL, Multiple and no diagnostic.
The asserted offset matches no candidate: Invalid (offset-mismatch), even in a gap with SHIFT_FORWARD.
The zone isn't in the rules: Unsupported (unknown-zone).
The wall time is within a day of either end of the rules' validity window: Unsupported (outside-rule-window).
ctx.resolve given anything but a ZonedIntent: TypeError.

entities.name: See an instant in a zone
entities.description: instant.in_zone(zone_id, ctx), the same as ctx.in_zone(instant, zone_id): the wall time in that zone at the instant, with the offset in force asserted.
entities.result: Unique(ZonedIntent), such as 2027-06-01T03:00:00-04:00[America/New_York].
failures: The zone isn't in the rules: Unsupported (unknown-zone).
The instant is outside the rules' validity window: Unsupported (outside-rule-window).
ctx.in_zone given anything but an Instant: TypeError.

entities.name: Order zoned values
entities.description: ctx.compare(a, b) for ZonedIntent, Instant and FixedOffsetDateTime values: zoned values are resolved strictly, then every candidate of a is compared with every candidate of b.
entities.result: Unique(Ordering) when only one order is possible; Multiple of the possible orders, in BEFORE, EQUAL, AFTER order, when it depends on which side of an overlap is meant. The diagnostics of resolving both sides are passed on.
failures: A side falls in a gap: NoneOf (gap).
A side's zone is unknown or outside the rules: Unsupported (unknown-zone, outside-rule-window).
A side's asserted offset contradicts the rules: Invalid (offset-mismatch).
Any other type: TypeError.

entities.name: Order two values of one type
entities.description: <, <=, > and >= on two CivilDate, CivilYearMonth, CivilTime, CivilDateTime, FixedOffsetDateTime or Instant values, through the JSON layer's compare. A missing second counts as 0, so 09:30 <= 09:30:00 holds both ways while 09:30 != 09:30:00.
entities.transport: comparison operator of the typed values
entities.result: A bool. Fixed-offset date-times order by the instant they name.
failures: The two values are of different types: TypeError (each side returns NotImplemented).
ZonedIntent has no comparison operators: TypeError. Use ctx.compare.

entities.name: Ask whether a range holds a point or meets another
entities.description: interval.contains(point) and interval.overlaps(other), in three-valued logic.
entities.result: Truth.DEFINITELY, POSSIBLY (an unknown end decides) or IMPOSSIBLE.

entities.name: Read the text form
entities.description: utv.parse(text) reads any text-form value and returns the type it describes; T.parse(text) narrows to one type. Bad text is an outcome, never an exception. str(value) is the way back.
entities.transport: exported function (utv.parse), and classmethod parse of each typed value
entities.result: Unique(value): 2026-11-05 a CivilDate, …Z an Instant, …+00:00 a FixedOffsetDateTime, …[Europe/Paris] a ZonedIntent, P1M a Period, [a, b) an Interval.
failures: Text outside the grammar: Invalid (syntax).
A field out of range: Invalid (day-out-of-range, month-out-of-range, field-out-of-range, offset-out-of-range).
Week dates, ordinal dates, basic format, decimal period components, EDTF qualifiers, an interval with no point: Unsupported (unsupported-form).
Second 60: Unsupported (leap-second); 24:00: Unsupported (end-of-day).
Any annotation but one [Area/Location], or a [zone] after Z or -00:00: Unsupported (unsupported-annotation).
Interval ends reversed: Invalid (reversed-interval); ends of different kinds or forms: Invalid (kind-mismatch).
T.parse given text of another type: Invalid (kind-mismatch).

entities.name: Read UTV JSON into a typed value
entities.description: utv.from_json(json) or T.from_json(json), from a dict or JSON text; value.to_json() is the way back.
entities.transport: exported function (utv.from_json), and classmethod from_json of each typed value
entities.result: Unique(value) when a typed value holds the JSON exactly; an explicit floating zone counts as no zone.
failures: JSON of the wrong shape, or text that isn't JSON: Invalid (malformed-value), followed by the 0.1 structural codes.
A value that can't exist: Invalid (day-out-of-range and the like).
T.from_json given another kind or form: Invalid (kind-mismatch).
A valid value no typed value holds exactly (a zoned date, a resolutionPolicy, provenance, a recurrence): Unsupported (unsupported-operand); the JSON layer still handles it.
Another well-formed utv/ version: Unsupported (unsupported-version).

entities.name: Bring a datetime value in
entities.description: utv.from_native(value[, intent]) turns a date, time, datetime or timedelta into a typed value, with the meaning the caller names.
entities.result: Unique(value): a CivilDate, CivilTime, CivilDateTime, Instant, FixedOffsetDateTime, ZonedIntent (with the offset of the datetime's fold asserted), PosixSeconds or Period.
failures: A naive datetime asked for an INSTANT, OFFSET or ZONED: Unsupported (local-zone).
A datetime with a fixed timezone and no intent, a timedelta with no intent, or an unknown intent: Invalid (intent-required).
ZoneInfo("localtime"), a file key, or a tzinfo class that is neither timezone nor ZoneInfo: Unsupported (local-zone).
A ZoneInfo wall time in a gap asked for an INSTANT or OFFSET: NoneOf (gap).
A time of day with a tzinfo, a fixed timezone asked for ZONED, a sub-second UTC offset, or a PERIOD with microseconds: Unsupported (unsupported-operand).
Anything but a date, time, datetime or timedelta: TypeError.

entities.name: Take a value out to datetime
entities.description: utv.to_native(value, tz=…, allow_loss=…) turns a typed value into a date, time, datetime or timedelta.
entities.result: Unique(native value); for a zoned value in an overlap with no asserted offset, Multiple of the fold-0 and fold-1 datetimes. With allow_loss=True a dropped part is reported as a precision-loss or zone-dropped warning.
failures: A year outside 1–9999: Unsupported (out-of-native-range).
Nanoseconds that aren't whole microseconds, without allow_loss: Unsupported (out-of-native-range).
A ZonedIntent without tz: Unsupported (needs-zone-rules); with allow_loss and an asserted offset, a fixed timezone and zone-dropped.
tz that isn't a ZoneInfo for the same zone id, or a tz for a floating or fixed-offset value: Unsupported (unsupported-operand).
A wall time the tz says doesn't exist: NoneOf (gap); an asserted offset the tz doesn't have there: Invalid (offset-mismatch).
A Period, ElapsedSeconds, CivilYearMonth or Interval: Unsupported (unsupported-operand).

entities.name: Build UTV JSON
entities.description: date, year_month, time, date_time, in_zone, with_offset, instant, period, posix_seconds, elapsed_seconds and interval (with UNBOUNDED and UNKNOWN) assemble the canonical everyday shapes as plain dicts. They don't judge the value: date(2026, 2, 30) is built, and operations report it.
entities.transport: exported function (utv.date and the other builders)
entities.result: A UTV JSON value (a dict).
failures: A field of the wrong Python type: TypeError.
interval with no point and no domain=: ValueError.

entities.name: Parse ISO 8601 text (JSON layer)
entities.description: parse_iso(text): ISO 8601 extended format, RFC 3339 and RFC 9557 forms into UTV JSON.
entities.result: A unique Result whose candidate is the value: a date, year-month, time, unzoned or fixed-offset date-time, zoned date-time (with offsetAssertion when an offset precedes the zone), or an instant for Z and -00:00.
failures: Not a str: invalid (malformed-value).
Outside the grammar, or -0000: invalid (syntax).
A field out of range: invalid (month-out-of-range, day-out-of-range, field-out-of-range, offset-out-of-range).
Week dates, ordinal dates, basic format: unsupported (unsupported-form).
Second 60: unsupported (leap-second); 24:00: unsupported (end-of-day).
Critical or other annotations, more than one, or a [zone] after Z or -00:00: unsupported (unsupported-annotation).

entities.name: Format ISO 8601 text (JSON layer)
entities.description: format_iso(value): the inverse of parse_iso for the everyday shapes.
entities.result: A unique Result whose candidate is the text; instants always print in UTC with seconds.
failures: A kind other than civil or instant: unsupported (unsupported-operand).
A zoned date, an offset that isn't whole minutes, or an instant fraction needing more than 9 digits: unsupported (no-text-form).
An invalid or malformed value: invalid, with its code.

entities.name: Parse the text form (JSON layer)
entities.description: parse_text(text): points as in parse_iso, ISO durations (P1M, -P1DT2H), bracket intervals with explicit endpoint state, and EDTF slash intervals on input.
entities.result: A unique Result whose candidate is the UTV value; operation parseText.
failures: Not a str: invalid (malformed-value).
Bad duration or interval syntax, '..' or '?' on a closed bracket, more than one '/': invalid (syntax).
Decimal period components, EDTF qualifiers or unspecified digits, an interval with no point: unsupported (unsupported-form).
Reversed ends: invalid (reversed-interval); ends of different kinds or forms: invalid (kind-mismatch).
Any failure of parse_iso for a point.

entities.name: Format the text form (JSON layer)
entities.description: format_text(value): the text form of a civil value, instant, calendar period or start-end interval.
entities.result: A unique Result whose candidate is the text; operation formatText.
failures: A period with mixed signs, components other than whole Y/M/W/D/H/M/S, a start-amount or amount-end interval, a reversed interval, second counts, and every other kind: unsupported (no-text-form).
Any failure of format_iso for a point.

entities.name: Derive date fields (JSON layer)
entities.description: fields(value) of a Gregorian date or date-time: dayOfWeek (Monday = 1), dayOfYear, isoWeekYear (a string), isoWeek, daysInMonth, isLeapYear.
entities.result: A unique Result whose candidate is the field object.
failures: A form other than date or datetime: unsupported (unsupported-operand).
A non-Gregorian calendar: unsupported (unsupported-calendar).
A date that doesn't exist: invalid (day-out-of-range).
Malformed input: invalid (malformed-value).

entities.name: Add an amount (JSON layer)
entities.description: add(value, amount[, policy]): years and months first, then the month-end rule, then weeks and days, then hours, minutes and seconds as wall-clock time. An instant takes only POSIX seconds, exactly.
entities.result: A unique Result with the new value; a dropped offsetAssertion is reported as offset-assertion-dropped (info).
failures: The day is missing from the target month under reject: none (month-end).
A second argument that isn't an amount, a calendar amount on an instant, a non-calendar amount on a civil value, or a component the form doesn't have: invalid (kind-mismatch).
SI seconds on an instant: unsupported (needs-leap-seconds).
A time of day, other kinds, fractional or unknown components: unsupported (unsupported-operand).
A monthEnd policy other than reject or constrain: unsupported (unsupported-policy).

entities.name: Compare two values (JSON layer)
entities.description: compare(a, b): before, equal or after, for unzoned civil values of one form, instants, and fixed-offset date-times.
entities.result: A unique Result whose candidate is "before", "equal" or "after".
failures: A value with a named zone: unsupported (needs-zone-rules): resolve first.
Different kinds or forms, or a floating value against one with an offset: unsupported (unsupported-operand).

entities.name: Count days (JSON layer)
entities.description: days_between(a, b): b − a in whole days, for two Gregorian dates.
entities.result: A unique Result whose candidate is an integer.
failures: Dates in different zones, or one zoned and one not: unsupported (different-zones).
A form other than date: unsupported (unsupported-operand).

entities.name: Measure between instants (JSON layer)
entities.description: posix_seconds_between(a, b): b − a as an exact POSIX-seconds amount.
entities.result: A unique Result whose candidate is a clock-ticks amount with a reduced rational.
failures: Anything but a tick-based unix-posix instant: unsupported (unsupported-operand).

entities.name: Relate a range and a point or range (JSON layer)
entities.description: contains(interval, point) and overlaps(a, b) on civil-date and instant intervals, in three-valued logic.
entities.result: A unique Result whose candidate is "definitely", "possibly" or "impossible".
failures: A first argument that isn't an interval: invalid (kind-mismatch).
Mixed domains, another domain, non-date civil points, or an interval that isn't start-end: unsupported (unsupported-operand).
Dates in different zones: unsupported (different-zones).

entities.name: Resolve a local date-time (JSON layer)
entities.description: resolve(value, rules[, policy]): a civil date-time to instant(s) under a rule bundle. Without a policy, the value's own resolutionPolicy applies, then reject for both.
entities.result: unique or multiple instants; manifest.dependencies names the rule set and loss is information-losing (zone, zoneIntent). A fixed-offset date-time resolves without rules.
failures: A form other than datetime: unsupported (unsupported-operand); second 60: unsupported (leap-second).
An unzoned date-time: symbolic (no-zone, info).
A zone not in the bundle: unsupported (unknown-zone); a wall time within a day of the window's edge: unsupported (outside-rule-window).
A policy value not implemented: unsupported (unsupported-policy).
An asserted offset that matches no candidate: invalid (offset-mismatch).
A gap: none (gap) unless shift-forward-by-gap; an overlap: multiple (ambiguous under reject).
A malformed rule bundle: invalid (malformed-value).

entities.name: Convert an instant to a zone or offset (JSON layer)
entities.description: to_zone(instant, zone_id, rules) and to_offset(instant, seconds): an instant as a civil date-time in a named zone (with offsetAssertion) or at a fixed offset.
entities.result: A unique Result with the date-time, always with second; to_zone's manifest names the rule set.
failures: A zone not in the bundle: unsupported (unknown-zone); an instant outside validFrom ≤ t < validUntil: unsupported (outside-rule-window).
to_offset with an offset beyond ±18:00: invalid (offset-out-of-range); one that isn't an int: invalid (malformed-value).

entities.name: Validate UTV JSON text
entities.description: validate_structural(text): the envelope and structure of one UTV JSON document against the bundled utv-1.0 schema.
entities.result: A Result with status valid, operation validate.
failures: A repeated object key: invalid (duplicate-key).
Text that isn't JSON, or NaN / Infinity: invalid (malformed-json).
Another well-formed version identifier, such as utv/1.1 or utv/2.0: unsupported (unsupported-version).
Any other schema identifier, such as utv/4: invalid (unknown-schema).
An unknown kind: invalid (unknown-kind); an unknown property: invalid (unknown-property); other schema violations: invalid with the keyword's code.

entities.name: Check a civil value's date
entities.description: validate_gregorian_date(text): after structural validation, whether the year, month and day of a proleptic Gregorian civil value name a real date. Any form with those fields is checked, month-day included.
entities.result: A Result with status valid.
failures: Any structural failure, as from validate_structural.
A kind other than civil: unsupported (unsupported-kind).
Another calendar: unsupported (unsupported-calendar).
Month outside 1–12: invalid (month-out-of-range); day outside the month: invalid (day-out-of-range).

entities.name: Convert a datetime value to UTV JSON
entities.description: from_date, from_time, from_datetime(dt[, intent]) and from_timedelta(td, intent) in utv.native: the JSON-level adapters under from_native.
entities.transport: exported function (utv.from_datetime and the other from_ adapters)
entities.result: A unique Result, operation convert, with the UTV value; an ambiguous ZoneInfo wall time adds ambiguous (info), and a ZONED wall time in a gap is kept without an asserted offset with a gap warning.
failures: As from_native: local-zone, intent-required, gap, unsupported-operand, TypeError.

entities.name: Convert UTV JSON to a datetime value
entities.description: to_date, to_time(value[, allow_loss]), to_datetime(value[, tz[, allow_loss]]) and to_timedelta(amount[, allow_loss]) in utv.native: the JSON-level adapters under to_native.
entities.transport: exported function (utv.to_datetime and the other to_ adapters)
entities.result: A Result, operation convert, whose candidates are datetime objects, with loss lossless, or information-losing naming the dropped fields.
failures: As to_native: out-of-native-range, needs-zone-rules, unsupported-operand, gap, offset-mismatch.
A calendar period to timedelta: unsupported (unsupported-operand).

relatedViews.relationship: The features these operations carry out.
The use cases that call them.
